thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — spike detected: kv-cache write amplification + cont-batch growth on route /v1/generate (region: us-west). error_rate: 7.2% -> 18% in 4m. latency p95 1.2s -> 4.8s. tagging oncall.
ashley: seeing continual kv key cardinality growth after the qwen-mqa deploy at 14:02 UTC. prefix cache size exploded on a subset of shards. multiple models showing sustained cont-batch windows > 80ms causing kv backpressure.
devon: on it. can you grab the cont-batch stats from the runtime? `curl -s http://runtime-metrics:9090/contbatch | jq .` — we need shard-level rates, prefetch hits, and eviction counts.
ashley: past 5m snapshot pasted below:
```
shard 3: cont_batch_window_ms=92, avg_batch_tokens=48, kv_write_rate=135/s, kv_evicts=420m/5m
shard 7: cont_batch_window_ms=110, avg_batch_tokens=61, kv_write_rate=210/s, kv_evicts=1.1k/5m
routes: llama-13b: 60% of requests; mistral-7b: 25%; qwen-mqa: 15%
prefix-cardinality (hot keys): increased 14x vs baseline
```
miguel: hmm qwen-mqa also shows degraded GQA->MQA demotion logic — prefetch strategy is promoting many prefixes into KV instead of sampling. possibly the new prefetch threshold param from rollback-2026-03-07 didn't land cleanly.
sam: customer-alert-bot: notifying impacted customers in tier-1 now (first batch). will update customers when we have mitigation. :alert:
devon: immediate mitigation options (fast):
- reduce cont-batch max_window_ms to 30ms on all cont-batch workers (low risk)
- disable prefetch for qwen-mqa routes (config flip)
- increase kv eviction aggressiveness (force TTL to 5m for hot prefixes)
- fallback routing: route qwen-mqa traffic to dedicated pool with LRU-only cache (slower cost but avoids noise)
Which do we want first?
ashley: do the config flips in that order. I can patch the runtime config and roll to one shard to validate.
devon: patching now — applying cont-batch max_window_ms=30 to shard 7 first. command: `kubectl -n runtime set env ds/contbatch WORKER_MAX_WINDOW_MS=30 --record`
kai: heads up, that env flip will restart pods on the daemonset. expect transient cold starts for those shards.
miguel: I'll disable qwen prefetch at the routing tier: `redwood-ctl routes update --route qwen-mqa --prefetch false`
ashley: applied cont-batch change on shard 7. metrics: cont_batch_window_ms dropped to 28ms, avg_batch_tokens down to 32, kv_write_rate dropped 48%. eviction spike still high but trending down.
sam: customer-alert-bot: update sent — "we're seeing degraded performance; mitigation in progress; no data loss expected."
devon: rolling change to shard 3 now. patching all remaining cont-batch workers.
ops-lead: can we also temporarily increase dedicated pool capacity? push to burst capacity (20%) for routes with SLA customers.
miguel: bumped dedicated pool for qwen-mqa and llama-13b to +25% for 20m window.
ashley: disabling qwen prefetch now.
miguel: prefetch disabled. prefetch hits -> 0, kv inserts from qwen down 92%. overall error_rate falling to 5%. p95 latency dropping to 1.6s.
devon: good signal. next: reduce kv eviction TTL back to normal after stabilization. sam, keep customers updated.
sam: will send follow-up in 10m. any ask for customer-facing notes?
ashley: quick note: root cause appears to be an interaction between the qwen-mqa prefetch promotion heuristics and cont-batch expansion heuristics — together they amplified prefix cardinality and forced aggressive eviction churn. also a config race in the rollback branch left prefetch threshold at a low value. will add issue to jira.
miguel: creating jira: RDW-INC-5227 "qwen prefetch threshold regression + cont-batch amplification". assigning to eng-ml and runtime.
devon: postmortem checklist:
- capture runtime traces for top 5 hot prefixes
- stash cont-batch config diffs and rollout history
- test prefetch thresholds against synthetic workload with high prefix branching
- add guardrail: if kv_insert_rate increases > 3x baseline in 5m, auto-disable prefetch for that route
- add canary for prefetch config changes (5% traffic)

ashley: I'll run the traces and attach to the jira. also proposing to add a runtime metric alert: cont_batch_window_ms > 50ms for >3m -> pager.
ops-lead: agree. Also schedule a 1hr follow-up with runtime, ml, and oncall to review fixes and rollout plan at 17:00 UTC.
sam: customers notified: "mitigations reduced errors and latency; we're monitoring; next update by 17:00 UTC."
kai: handing off to next on-call (devon) for monitoring. handoff notes:
- mitigations applied: cont-batch max_window_ms=30 -> cluster-wide
- qwen prefetch disabled
- dedicated pool bump +25% for critical routes (expires in 20m)
- jira RDW-INC-5227 created (link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RDW-INC-5227)
- customer updates sent
devon: thanks. I'll hold until 17:00 UTC and then coordinate rollback of bursts if stable. if error_rate climbs back >8% re-escalate.
ops-lead: great work team — please add any outstanding logs/traces to the jira. closing thread but keeping it pinned for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
ashley: moving logs to jira and will draft blameless postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigations applied). final metrics snapshot: error_rate 1.1%, p95 latency 1.3s, kv_write_rate baseline restored.
devon: handoff complete to devon for monitoring shift.
